newsitem.title: USA: In court, Goldman's father talks of murdered son.
newsitem.headline: In court, Goldman's father talks of murdered son.

text.p: Choking back tears, Ron Goldman's father Fred told the jury in the O.J. Simpson civil trial Monday about his relationship with his son who was murdered along with Simpson's ex-wife.
Goldman, the last witness for the plaintiffs, spoke in a shaky voice as family photos of him and his son were projected onto a screen in the courtroom with Simpson looking on from the defence table.
"We were always close, there was something special about our relationship. Whatever happened, it was a bond that never dissipated," Goldman told his attorney Daniel Petrocelli.
Simpson, an ex-football star-turned actor, was acquitted in criminal court last year of murdering Ron Goldman and Nicole Brown Simpson.
He has been sued in civil court by the victims' families who contend he is responsible for the deaths and should pay damages.

Speaking about the loss of his only son, Fred Goldman's voice wavered several times when he recalled taking the young Ron and his sister Kim on a surprise vacation to Acapulco, Mexico, and when he talked about taking his son to meetings of Indian Guides (a YMCA group for fathers and sons) and Little League baseball games.
His testimony concluded five weeks of the plaintiffs' case and the defence was expected to begin arguing its case later Monday.
